name: John XXII condemns Spiritual Franciscans
summary: The bull Ad conditorem canonum (1322) and Cum inter nonnullos (1323) reject the absolute-poverty doctrine of the Spiritual Franciscans, holding that Christ and the apostles owned property. Several Spirituals (including Michael of Cesena and William of Ockham) flee to Bavaria under Louis IV's protection.

_quarry.structural_significance: Definitive late-medieval papal rejection of apostolic-poverty absolutism; the resulting Franciscan-papal conflict feeds into Marsilius of Padua's anti-papal political theory.
